title: Finding faults in a cumin seed
odia:
ଋଷି ଘରକୁ ମହାଋଷି ଗଲେ
ଜିରା ଭିତରୁ ଶିରା କାଢିଲେ।
literal_meaning: A great sage went to a sage’s house and drew a vein out of cumin.
meaning_odia: ଜିରା ଭଳି ଛୋଟ ଜିନିଷରୁ ଶିରା କାଢ଼ିବା ଚିତ୍ରରେ ଅଯଥା ଦୋଷ ଖୋଜିବାକୁ ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗ କରାଯାଇଛି। ଋଷିଙ୍କ ଘରକୁ ମହାଋଷି ଆସିବାର କଥା ଏହି ଖୁଣ ଧରିବାକୁ ଆହୁରି ନାଟକୀୟ କରେ।
explanation: The tiny cumin seed becomes the object of an extravagant search for faults. An inspected idiom gloss explains drawing a vein from cumin as needless fault-finding. Read through that idiom, the visiting great sage turns supposed distinction into an occasion for petty criticism.
usage_example: A reviewer ignores the substance of a sound proposal and keeps raising trivial objections. Someone could use the couplet to question that fault-finding. This illustration is newly composed.
cultural_context: The progression from sage to great sage raises expectations of wisdom. The second line reduces the visitor’s achievement to extracting something minute from cumin. That contrast supplies the editorial reading of exaggerated discernment becoming pettiness.
